evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game is a foundational capability and does not inherently require another backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting via a game URL inherently depends on a game existing to generate/provide that URL.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes an existing game/session context to start the round within.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing items for a session depends on items being created/added to that session.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item inherently requires that items already exist in the session.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item to a list for estimation presupposes an existing game/session to hold that list.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item depends on items having been created/added first.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item depends on items existing in the list first.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates presupposes that estimates can be given/collected in a round.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average inherently depends on estimates having been provided and available to average.

evaluations.evidence: filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling based on all estimators' cards depends on the capability for estimators to submit/show cards (estimates).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate depends on a round with estimates/discussion context already occurring.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating earlier items depends on having previously estimated items in the same session.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories implies there is a destination game/session backlog/list to import into.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/pasting stories implies an existing game/session list to paste into.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games can be implemented as a standalone listing feature over stored games; it does not inherently require another specific story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript inherently depends on games (and their data) existing to view.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the existence of a transcript to export.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the existence of a transcript to export.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game inherently depends on games existing to be deleted.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is self-contained and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in inherently depends on accounts existing (created beforehand).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details inherently depends on an existing account (and typically being able to access it).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account inherently depends on an account existing.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a cross-cutting presentation requirement and does not inherently depend on a specific other story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders inherently depend on accounts (with stored email/credentials) existing.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an estimation scale presupposes that estimation rounds/cards exist in the game to apply the scale to.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: This is an extension of inviting estimators and depends on the base invite capability.

evaluations.evidence: join a game ... on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a received URL inherently depends on the game being created and the invite/URL being provided.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item depends on items being created/selected for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items depends on items existing in the session list.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This depends on the capability for estimators to join and submit estimates in a round.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates ... after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates after everyone has estimated depends on estimators being able to join the game and provide estimates.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until ... all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on the existence of an estimation/draw mechanism where estimates are submitted and later revealed.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Prior estimates can only exist if estimating has occurred and estimates are stored per estimator/story.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: This depends on estimates being given and tracked during a round.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared countdown timer can be implemented as a standalone feature within the game UI without inherently requiring another specific story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself
evaluations.rationale: Resetting 'the two-minute timer' inherently depends on the timer feature existing.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds depends on rounds having occurred and their stories/estimates being available.

evaluations.evidence: cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering across draws presupposes that draws/estimation cards exist.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on an estimation/draw mechanism where estimates are submitted and a draw can be completed.

evaluations.evidence: thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a photo near played cards depends on the existence of the card-playing/estimation interaction.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: A glossary can be created independently of other functional stories.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing can be implemented independently as a technical improvement without requiring another specific story to be completed first.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Predictable URLs are a self-contained design/UX requirement and do not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages can be implemented independently as a cross-cutting UI feature without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Storing results non-identifiably presupposes that results/estimates are being stored at all.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Usage metrics inherently depend on the game being used and usage data being generated/recorded by core gameplay features.
